headline: Approved prior meeting minutes; heard a fiscal recovery presentation on pensions, debt, and possible state assistance for Hamden.
summary: Walter Morton presented on Hamden's fiscal condition and possible solutions, including state-backed financial assistance. Members also discussed the commission's role, possible task forces, and school transportation concerns. Members approved the minutes of the August 6, 2026 meeting by a 4-0 vote, with two members absent.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Finance Commission Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
6:00 PM, September 3, 2026 
  
 
Memorial Town Hall 
2372 Whitney Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL OF THE MEETING AND TAKING OF THE ROLL   
 The meeting was called to order by Chair Commissioner R. Scolnic at 6:01 PM. 
 
The Clerk called the roll, and the following members were: 
 
Present: 
 
Commissioner Rabbi Benjamin Scolnic, Chair 
Commissioner Michael Martin 
Commissioner Arnold Margolis 
Commissioner Thomas Fortuna 
 
Absent: 
Commissioner Myles Carter-Solomon, Youth 
Commissioner Bethany McCluster 
 
Also in attendance were Walter Morton and Dr. Mario Ciccarini, Hamden Board of 
Education Member; Briana J. Belton-Robinson, Boards and Commissions Clerk; and 10 
members of the public joining virtually. 
2. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 Chairman R. Scolnic requested a motion to adopt the minutes from Thursday, August 6th, 
2026. 
 
The motion was made by T. Fortuna and seconded by Commissioner M. Martin. 
Vote by Roll Call: 
 
Yes 
Commissioner R. Scolnic  
Commissioner A. Margolis 
Commissioner M. Martin 
Commissioner T. Fortuna 
 
No 
 
Absent 
Commissioner B. McCluster
Commissioner M. Carter-Solomon, Youth 
 
The motion passed. 
 
• Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 4, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 2 
 
3. PUBLIC INPUT SESSION   
 Dr. Mario Ciccarini of the Hamden Board of Education asked about the Finance 
Commission's role and authority in the Town of Hamden. 
 
Chairman R. Scolnic stated that the Finance Commission has “no teeth” under the Town 
Charter and that there remains uncertainty regarding the scope of the Commission’s role 
and authority. 
 
Commissioner T. Fortuna said the previous Finance Commission had walked away and 
expressed concern that the current Commission may also be approaching a point where 
members consider abandoning it. 
 
Commissioner T. Fortuna further stated that, in his view, the current Town administration is 
focused on “keeping the lights on.” He discussed an assumption that Town officials may be 
anticipating a default that could result in intervention or takeover by the State of 
Connecticut. 
 
Chairman R. Scolnic discussed efforts to establish a task force and/or long-range planning 
committee. He stated that he had previously spoken with the Town Attorney, who indicated 
that a clerk would be required to be present in order for the task force and long-range 
planning committee to formally convene and meet. The Commission subsequently 
contacted the Town Clerk’s Office and was advised that a clerk could not be provided. 
 
Michael Meeley, a concerned Hamden resident, addressed the Commission regarding the 
financial burden of property taxes on homeowners. Mr. Meeley urged the Town to consider 
seeking a bailout from the State of Connecticut to lessen the tax burden on homeowners. 
He also expressed interest in participating in any future committees established to address 
the Town’s financial condition. 
4. REPORT FROM EX-OFFICIO MEMBERS   
 Chair Scolnic noted that the Commission had received consistent participation from the 
Board of Education and some participation from the Mayor’s Office. He expressed concern 
about the lack of representation from the Legislative Council and said he had contacted the 
Council President and the Chair of its Finance Committee about participation. The Finance 
Commission agenda identifies representatives of the Mayor, Board of Education, and 
Legislative Council budget committee as ex officio members. 
  1. Public Official or municipal employee representing the Mayor, designated by the 
Mayor.  
  No report was provided by a representative designated by the Mayor. 
  2. Representative of the Board of Education, designated by a majority vote of said Board
The Board of Education representative reported that the Board’s next meeting was 
scheduled for September 8, 2026. The Board held a retreat on August 14, during 
which members worked with the Superintendent and Assistant Superintendent to 
develop draft Board goals for further consideration. 
 
The representative reported that the school year began with positions largely filled 
and that some employees displaced as a result of budgetary issues had been brought 
back as other openings became available. 
Concerns were raised regarding school transportation at the beginning of the 
academic year, including students not being picked up as scheduled and experiencing 
lengthy trips home. The representative stated that the matter would be raised at the 
upcoming Board meeting to determine the cause of the transportation issues and 
whether corrective measures were being implemented. 
The Commission also discussed school funding priorities and the limited amount of 
discretionary funding within school district budgets. The Board representative 
explained that salaries, transportation, and purchased services account for significant 
portions of the budget and that discretionary accounts may be frozen when other 
areas exceed projections. 
Discussion also occurred regarding competitive grant funding. The representative 
reported that Hamden had applied for, but did not receive, a recent competitive state 
grant for additional special education funding. The representative intended to inquire 
whether the district had received feedback regarding its application so that the 
information could inform future grant submissions. 
 
  3. Chair of the Legislative Council committee of jurisdiction over the budget or a 
member of said committee designated by the Chair  
  No report was provided by the Chair of the Legislative Council Budget Committee or 
their designee. 
5. UPDATE REPORT FROM THE MUNICIPAL BOARD AND COMMISSIONS, INVITED 
GUEST   
 
 
 1. Walter Morton, Director of Government & Community Affairs and Government 
Relations for Connecticut Energy Marketers Association (CEMA) 
       
  Mr. Walter Morton provided a presentation regarding Hamden’s current fiscal 
condition, contributing factors, potential solutions, and examples of municipalities that 
have undergone fiscal recovery. The meeting agenda identifies Mr. Morton as the 
invited guest for this portion of the meeting. 
 
Mr. Morton stated that he reviewed historical Town budgets, audits, financial reports, 
archival materials, and other records to examine the development of Hamden’s 
financial condition. He discussed the historical underfunding of the Town’s pension 
obligations and other financial decisions that, in his assessment, contributed to the 
Town’s current fiscal challenges.
Mr. Morton reviewed Hamden’s Fiscal Year 2026–2027 finances. His presentation 
identified a total budget of $327,811,161, a 53.67 mill rate, approximately $32.55 
million in Town and Board of Education debt service, a $28.8 million actuarially 
determined legacy pension contribution, and approximately $60 million in medical 
costs. 
 
Mr. Morton identified several contributing factors to the Town’s fiscal condition, 
including the lack of a Town-wide master plan, historical underfunding of pensions, 
retirement packages, the 2015 Pension Obligation Bonds, fiscal management 
practices, stagnant Grand List growth, and investment strategy. 
 
Mr. Morton also reviewed the Town’s existing debt service, debt-per-capita ranking, 
Equalized Grand List per capita, and projected legacy pension contributions. The 
materials presented to the Commission showed increasing projected employer 
pension contributions through 2044, followed by a substantial decrease in 2045. 
 
Mr. Morton presented several potential solutions for consideration, including 
development of a long-term Hamden Master Plan involving the Mayor, Legislative 
Council, and Board of Education; seeking state-backed financial assistance; engaging 
the Connecticut State Treasurer regarding pension management; engaging the 
Connecticut State Comptroller regarding medical insurance costs; developing a Town-
wide economic development plan; establishing a Board of Education strategic plan; 
and examining opportunities to consolidate Town and Board of Education services. 
 
Mr. Morton presented case studies involving Springfield, Massachusetts; Chelsea, 
Massachusetts; and Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. He discussed how these municipalities 
addressed significant fiscal challenges through combinations of state assistance or 
oversight, professional financial management, operational reforms, long-term financial 
planning, pension and expenditure reforms, and economic development. 
 
Mr. Morton stated that successful municipal recoveries shared several characteristics, 
including a candid assessment of financial conditions, conditional outside assistance, 
multiyear financial planning, professional financial capacity, action on long-term 
liabilities, protection of core services, economic and tax-base renewal, and sustained 
oversight and public reporting. 
 
Mr. Morton concluded that Hamden should consider pursuing relief through a state-
local recovery arrangement in which immediate assistance would be accompanied by 
a credible path toward structural balance, pension sustainability, stronger financial 
management, and Grand List growth. He stated that long-term success should include 
the Town’s ability to meet pension obligations, maintain core services, invest in 
infrastructure, grow the Grand List, and remain affordable without recurring 
emergency measures. 
 
The Commission thanked Mr. Morton for his presentation and discussed the Town’s 
long-term financial obligations, potential state assistance, pension costs, economic 
development, and the importance of comprehensive long-term planning. 
6. UPDATE REPORT FROM THE FINANCE COMMISSION CHAIR
Chair R. Scolnic discussed the Commission’s role as an advisory body and its efforts to 
facilitate communication among the Town administration, Legislative Council, Board of 
Education, and other municipal entities. 
 
The Commission discussed efforts to establish smaller working groups or task forces to 
examine municipal spending and long-range planning. Members discussed procedural 
requirements associated with convening such meetings, including the need for appropriate 
clerical support and compliance with Freedom of Information requirements. 
Chair R. Scolnic reiterated the importance of long-range planning while addressing the 
Town’s immediate fiscal challenges. Members discussed the need for cooperation among 
municipal bodies and expressed concern regarding obstacles that had delayed additional 
meetings and collaborative efforts. 
The Commission also discussed information concerning anticipated financial pressures on 
residents and the potential effects of broader economic and governmental changes on the 
Town and its residents. 
 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No Executive Session was held. 
8. REGULAR AGENDA   
 No additional matters were discussed. 
9. UNFINISHED BUSINESS   
 No unfinished business was discussed. 
10. NEW BUSINESS   
 No new business was discussed. 
11. ADJOURNMENT   
 
A motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. 
The motion passed unanimously. 
The Finance Commission meeting was adjourned at approximately 7:15 PM.
